director.chapterArc: Arrival at Meridian: The group endures decontamination and registration; Toren confesses to killing a Riftspawn; Rook reveals his true name (Elias Marsh) and the truth about their conditional admittance; they are watched, not feared.
director.restraintNote: Maintain an analytical distance. Do not dramatize the bureaucratic horror or the emotional weight of the confession beyond what Toren's sensory experience dictates. The tension is in the silence between questions and answers.

cues.delivery: Measured observation of time passing; the weight of waiting is felt in the pacing.
cues.from: The gate took twenty-six minutes, and Toren could not decide whether that was cruelty or just what happened to a place above a certain size — whether it stopped having the sort of insides where the difference could still be found.
cues.through: They counted it because Dessa counted it. She sat down on the wet road at the ninety-foot mark with her leg out and her boots full of ash and said, "Right, I'm timing this," in a voice with something badly wrong in it, and then she timed it, out loud, in minutes, the whole way.
cues.reason: Establishes the scene's oppressive atmosphere without rushing into action.

cues.delivery: Clinical description of the guards; flat delivery to contrast with Toren's expectation of help.
cues.from: At twenty-six the gate opened, and what came out of it was not help.
cues.through: Four people came out in sealed grey coats with the hoods up and the faces behind flat panels, moving at a fast walk in a line abreast, and they went straight past the tailgate with Senna Voss on it and straight past a boy sitting in the road who could not stand up, and they went to Dessa's cooking pot.
cues.reason: The arrival is not a rescue but an inspection.

cues.delivery: Dessa's dialogue delivered with urgent logic; the guards' responses are flat and procedural.
cues.through: "Yes, ma'am, and I need you to step away from it, and then I need your boots."
cues.reason: Highlighting the disconnect between Toren's value of ash and the station's protocol.

cues.delivery: Senna's answers are factual; the narrator maintains distance from her trauma.
cues.from: Then, and only then, two of them went back through the gate and came out again with a stretcher, and did the thing that Toren had been walking three hundred miles toward for four months, which was that a woman in a grey coat knelt down in a road beside Senna Voss and put a hand on her wrist and said, "All right, my love. What year did it happen?"
cues.through: "The old plant at Caul Hill. I was — " she took the breath she had to go some distance for " — I was fifty-three and I went in for the copper, and I knew what was in there, and so did every other soul on that crew, and we went in anyway because it was copper."
cues.reason: The medical intake is a ritual of survival, not drama.

cues.delivery: Rook's relief is internalized; his voice remains steady despite the emotional release.
cues.from: The woman in the grey coat wrote it down. Then she said, "You've been carried a long way, haven't you," and Senna said, "By a great many people who could have done something else," and that was the last thing Toren heard her say for two days.
cues.through: "They took her in, and there were proper instruments in that woman's hands, and she asked the right question first and she asked it in the right order, and I have been frightened for four months that this place wouldn't be what it said it was." Rook had his head back against the berm and his eyes shut and the rain going onto his face. "It's what it said it was. Everything that happens from here is a different kind of problem and I'll take every single one of them."
cues.reason: Restraint in Rook's reaction emphasizes the gravity of their survival.

cues.delivery: Wyck's dialogue is dry and observational; Toren's internal monologue is analytical.
cues.from: They were in it for two hours and it was the warmest two hours any of them had had in a fortnight, because there were pipes running along the wall behind the bench, and the pipes were hot, and nobody had told them the pipes would be hot. Wyck put his back against them and shut his eyes and said, "Oh," in a completely undefended voice, and did not speak again for twenty minutes.
cues.through: "It's got a roof at that end."
cues.reason: The contrast between the cold yard and the warm pipes grounds the scene.

cues.delivery: Hallet's introduction is matter-of-fact; Toren's dislike is noted as a fact.
cues.from: His name was Ivor Hallet. He gave it at once, unprompted, the way you give a thing that is going to be on a document anyway, and he was about forty-five, and he had a grey cardigan on under an oilskin and a pen on a string round his neck, and he was not unkind at any point in the next two hours, and Toren disliked him with a clean and total intensity for approximately eleven years.
cues.through: "Five," said Toren again, and heard his own voice do something, and Dessa put her hand flat on his back between the shoulder blades the way Senna did, and left it there.
cues.reason: Establishing the bureaucratic antagonist without villainizing him.

cues.delivery: Rook's name reveal is delivered with quiet finality; no dramatic pause needed.
cues.reason: The weight of the name 'Elias Marsh' lands in its simplicity.

cues.delivery: Hallet's reaction is professional; Rook's explanation of 'referred' is calm.
cues.from: Ivor Hallet wrote it down. Then he stopped writing. Then he turned back a very large number of pages in a very large book, and went down a column with the pen held above the paper the way a man does when he already knows, and found the place, and looked at it.
cues.through: "I don't," said Ivor Hallet, "and I would if I could."
cues.reason: The revelation of the past is handled with bureaucratic precision.

cues.delivery: Hallet's explanation of the register is clear and unadorned; Dessa's objection is logical.
cues.from: "Declaration of capability," said Hallet, and laid four buff cards on the ledge inside the window, and did not push them through. "This is where I'm required to tell you exactly what this is before you fill one in, and I'm required to tell you that you may decline. So. Meridian keeps a register of Kindled persons inside the line. It's not a secret register, you can go and look at your own entry any Tuesday, and there's about eleven hundred names in it. If you're Kindled and you're inside this berm, you're expected to be on it.
cues.through: "Yes, miss," said Ivor Hallet. "It is. I'd write that down too if there were a column for it."
cues.reason: The rules are presented as facts, not threats.

cues.delivery: Wyck's question is direct; Hallet's reassurance about Senna is firm.
cues.from: Wyck said, "Does she get treated either way?"
cues.reason: The priority of medical care over registration rules.

cues.delivery: Wyck and Rook's card writing is described with rhythmic slowness; the silence between actions.
cues.from: Wyck wrote for a long time and then crossed most of it out.
cues.reason: The weight of their choices in filling out the forms.

cues.delivery: Hallet's reading of the cards is detached; Toren's confession is delivered with surprising calm.
cues.from: Toren did not see the card. He saw the length of time it took and he saw Ivor Hallet read it through the window and put it down and read it again, and then look up, over the top of it, through the glass, at a man sitting on a bench in a wet coat with a hole through his back.
cues.through: Rook, on the bench, did not move and did not look at anybody, and it occurred to Toren afterward that the man had given them a rule in a road and had then sat in a concrete yard and let it run without touching it, because a rule you touch is not a rule.
cues.reason: The admission of killing a Riftspawn is treated as a fact.

cues.delivery: Hallet's questions are precise; Toren's answers are factual.
cues.from: "The question's got a name on it," said Ivor Hallet, after a moment. "I'll read that as well, because you'd have it out of me sooner or later. The party reports a boy of thirteen. Confirm."
cues.through: "Everybody in this place is keeping a record," said Wyck Tanner, "and I've been here four hours."
cues.reason: The interrogation is a formality of the station.

cues.delivery: Rook's final speech to Toren is delivered with quiet conviction; the ending is still.
cues.from: Toren went and stood outside the long building at the north end at about the eleventh hour, because Dessa had found out where it was and told him without being asked, which was the kindest thing anybody did for him that week.
cues.through: "You got her here. That's done. Nobody can take it off you and it's not conditional on anything and it's not reviewable in a fortnight, and whatever it turns out to have cost — and it's going to cost, and I don't know the number yet either — it is the only thing any of us set out to do, and it is done, and you did it."
cues.reason: The resolution of their immediate crisis.

pauses.after: The gate took twenty-six minutes, and Toren could not decide whether that was cruelty or just what happened to a place above a certain size — whether it stopped having the sort of insides where the difference could still be found.
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the nature of waiting; allows listener to absorb the atmosphere.

pauses.after: At twenty-six the gate opened, and what came out of it was not help.
pauses.reason: Brief pause before revealing the guards' arrival is not a rescue.

pauses.after: "It's eleven pounds of lifted ash, it's — there's four hundred pounds more of it in a road three miles back, there's a year of it out there, it's—"
pauses.reason: Pause after Dessa's desperate explanation to let the procedural rejection land.

pauses.after: The woman in the grey coat wrote it down. Then she said, "You've been carried a long way, haven't you," and Senna said, "By a great many people who could have done something else," and that was the last thing Toren heard her say for two days.
pauses.reason: Major pause for Toren's emotional reaction; a moment of grief and relief.
Emphasizes the physical relief of warmth after months of cold.

pauses.after: "It's got a roof at that end."
pauses.reason: Breath before the description of Hallet enters the scene.

pauses.before: How many of you are there.
pauses.reason: Prepares for the count that defines their group identity.

pauses.after: "Five," said Toren again, and heard his own voice do something, and Dessa put her hand flat on his back between the shoulder blades the way Senna did, and left it there.
pauses.reason: Pause for Toren's internal reaction to his own voice; a moment of self-awareness.
Highlights Toren's self-awareness in a moment of stress.
Pause after the name reveal 'Elias Marsh' to let its significance sink in.

pauses.after: "I found out at the time," said Rook. "I stood at a window at the top of a stair for four hours on the second day and a very polite young woman told me the word means it's gone to the right place. And it had. That's the part nobody ever believes. It had gone to precisely the right place and it is still there." He had not moved and his voice had not changed at all. "Write the name. I've no quarrel with you, Mr Hallet, and I'd like that in the book as well if you keep a column for it."
pauses.reason: Brief pause before Hallet's final response about his inability to write it down.

pauses.before: I found out at the time
pauses.reason: Prepares for Rook's revelation of his past knowledge.

pauses.after: "That's not a choice," said Dessa. "That's the same thing said twice with a bad face on one of them."
pauses.reason: Pause after Dessa's sharp observation that the choice isn't real; emphasizes her logic.

pauses.after: "I don't do anything, that's the whole of the — " He stopped. He looked at his own strapped hand, and flexed the three fingers that could not feel anything, which he had done four hundred times a day for four months. Then he wrote one line and turned the card over so nobody could read it, and only years afterward, in a different room, did Toren find out that it had said I don't fall over, in Wyck Tanner's flat square hand, with nothing else on the card at all.
pauses.reason: Major pause for Wyck's internal realization about his card; a moment of quiet dignity.

pauses.before: it had said I don't fall over,
pauses.reason: Emphasizes the stark simplicity and dignity of Wyck's entry.
Pause after Rook writes the truth; allows time to process the weight of his choice.
Marks the decisive moment of Rook choosing truth over safety.
Major pause for Toren's confession; a moment where he steps into the light.
Sets up the specific accusation that Toren must answer.
Isolates Toren's admission of responsibility for the killing.

pauses.after: Ivor Hallet wrote all of it. It took him some time. He did not ask a single follow-up question, which Toren noticed, and which he did not understand for another four days, when it was explained to him that a man at an intake window does not ask follow-up questions about a thing that is going to be asked about again by somebody else.
pauses.reason: Pause after Hallet stops asking questions; emphasizes his professional detachment.

pauses.after: "Because here's what's in that book now. There is an old woman in that building being treated, and there's four of us on a register, and somewhere behind us there's four hundred pounds of the best ash anybody at this wall has seen in ten years lying in a road that their own people won't go out to in the dark. And on a sheet in a drawer it says that the thing that made it was put down by a boy of thirteen who has been Ember since the spring." He looked up at the long dark roofline. "They're not frightened of what came out of the Sag, Toren. They've got a procedure for what comes out of the Sag. They've had one for sixty years."
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing on the realization that they are not feared but watched; a heavy beat for Toren's understanding.
Prepares for Rook's crucial distinction between fear and caution.
